items.title: How Experienced Developers Use AI Agents
AI Agent Use for Coding in 2025
Metrics Playground
items.detailHtml: A hands-on playground for metrics and evaluation workflows aimed at Cyber D&M engineers, focused on how agentic software development changes instrumentation, feedback loops, and what we choose to measure. I built the whole thing using agentic tooling like GitHub Copilot to walk the talk, showing how these tools invite low-stakes experimentation and make it way easier to spin up interactive prototypes without a ton of overhead. The playground itself includes interactive data tables with inline editing, JSON view toggles, and batch operations, giving engineers a real sandbox to explore and validate metadata without jumping between tools.

items.title: Admin Metrics Dashboard
items.detailHtml: An in-house admin dashboard for cyber log monitoring, designed to replace a Grafana-heavy setup with views tuned to our operators' workflows, alert semantics, and day-to-day triage habits. This was the first iteration of a custom monitoring system built in React, TypeScript, and Python. We added dynamic timeframe filtering, real-time threshold alerting, and granular inventory tracking across >5k assets, so admins could actually catch anomalies instead of scrolling through pages of widgets that lack customizability.

items.title: ILM Portal
items.detailHtml: A centralized identity and lifecycle management portal that brings together all the plugins our team was building under one roof instead of bouncing between disconnected tools. I led the end-to-end design on this one, serving as the point of contact for all UX concerns and ensuring the experience held together as we onboarded new plugins. One of the bigger ones it housed was a toxic access pairs plugin I helped redesign, which flagged dangerous permission combinations and cut security vulnerabilities by 40%.

items.title: File Upload Tool
items.detailHtml: A file upload and validation path for native content feeding IAM analytics — checking format, completeness, and consistency before data lands in downstream reporting and access models. The big upgrade here was translating an existing Python validation script into our Java codebase and wiring up real-time error feedback through Angular, so users could see exactly what was wrong with their file before resubmitting instead of waiting on a manual review cycle. That alone cut processing time by about 2 hours per upload and completely eliminated duplicate submissions.

items.title: Penetration Test Checklists
items.detailHtml: A remediation platform workflow for offensive security that imports Excel files and renders them as editable spreadsheets in the browser, so testers could track progress, assign work across the team, and export updated penetration test checklists without bouncing between static files and side channels—pulling import, collaboration, and export into one surface instead of a patchwork of local copies. I built the experience in React and TypeScript, focusing on faithful imports and spreadsheet-like editing so the UI stayed usable during live engagements, which kept mid-engagement checklist edits on-platform instead of re-roundtripping every change through Excel.

items.title: Capital One
items.detailHtml: I built and maintained internal platforms focused on cybersecurity visibility and access management. For PDQM, I developed custom monitoring dashboards and data quality tooling using React, TypeScript, Python, and Angular—replacing third-party solutions, building security heatmap visualizations, and engineering performance optimizations that cut processing times and cloud infrastructure costs significantly. On Access Vikings, I led frontend development for access request tooling and identity management plugins using AngularJS and Java, redesigned security-critical features like toxic access pair detection, and drove design system adoption across the platform. Across both teams, I also contributed to developer experience improvements including CI/CD testing integrations, documentation, and ML-powered support automation.

items.title: Various Companies
items.detailHtml: Before full-time work I spent a few years at the intersection of technology and public interest—across editorial, data, and policy roles. At the Council on Foreign Relations I did editorial research supporting foreign policy coverage, contributing to graphics and analysis on topics ranging from Latin American vaccination efforts and border wall construction to global nuclear energy generation, LGBTQ+ rights expansions, and vice presidential history. At New America's Digital Impact and Governance Initiative I focused on tech policy research, writing about integrated data systems and examining platforms like New York's workforce development portal as case studies in how governments deliver services digitally. At ActBlue I worked on data analysis and data engineering on the progressive fundraising platform.

items.title: University of Central Florida
items.detailHtml: Across three years of undergraduate research I worked in political instability, adolescent online safety, and applied machine learning. With Jonathan Powell, I helped build an early-warning forecasting platform that estimated monthly coup risk for >200 countries, wiring data pipelines that fed internal reports and public-facing analysis that reached over 500k readers a year; the same thread of work also showed up as commentary for Just Security and Political Violence at a Glance. With Pamela Wisniewski, I coded 50k Instagram DMs into an ecologically valid dataset for training models that flag online risks among teens, then ran an independent project comparing qualitative annotation of text summarization models at scale. With Amy Donley, I led a systematic literature review on COVID-19 and substance abuse in underserved populations, synthesizing risk factors across demographic groups to support evidence-based interventions.

items.title: XR Access
items.detailHtml: I led frontend development using React.js, TypeScript, and Material UI to build accessible, interactive interfaces for a lab focused on creating new technologies and tools for disabled users. My work included designing and running usability studies for web applications that help blind and low-vision users navigate unfamiliar desktop interfaces through audio spatialization, as well as building a React Native mobile app used in a 20-person study that uncovered new categories of assistive technology for fostering connection between sighted and blind and low-vision users.

items.title: University of Washington Tacoma
items.detailHtml: Computational research at the intersection of topology, statistics, and machine learning to identify communities of interest for fairer political redistricting and better representation of marginalized groups in the United States. This involved building data pipelines in Python (Pandas, NumPy) to process and flag datasets at the block group level, compute summary statistics for detected districts, and lead dimensionality reduction analysis using SVD/PCA on multivariate datasets.

items.title: Bachelor of Science
items.detailHtml: Three years of undergraduate research spanning political instability, adolescent online safety, and applied machine learning. Took courses across ethnographic methods, research design, and computer science. I helped build an early-warning forecasting platform with Jonathan Powell that estimated monthly coup risk for >200 countries and designed data pipelines that fed internal reports and public-facing articles that reached over 500k readers a year; I also coded 50k Instagram DMs into an ecologically valid dataset to help train models for detecting online risks among teens with Pamela Wisniewski, which led to an independent project comparing the qualitative annotation of text summarization models at scale. Alongside this, I led a systematic literature review on COVID-19's effects on substance abuse in underserved populations with Amy Donley, identifying risk factors across demographic groups to support evidence-based interventions.
